hook: Did You Know Your 'Deleted' Files Are Never Truly Erased?
headline: Your Deleted Files Are Never Actually Erased From Your Hard Drive

slides.speaker: vr
slides.title: Deleted Files Stay? 🤯
slides.bubble: Did you know 'deleted' files are never truly gone from your hard drive?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Just the Pointer 🗺️
slides.bubble: Yep! Your computer just removes the address pointer in its file system, not the actual data.

slides.speaker: vr
slides.title: Invisible Data? 👻
slides.bubble: So, the data is still sitting there, taking up space, just... invisible to me?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Library Analogy 📚
slides.bubble: Imagine a library book's index card is removed. The book is still physically on the shelf!

slides.speaker: vr
slides.title: Recovery Risk? 🚨
slides.bubble: So, someone could potentially recover my old 'deleted' personal documents or photos? That's scary!

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Until Overwritten ✍️
slides.bubble: Yes, until new information physically writes over those exact sectors, recovery is often possible!

slides.speaker: byte
slides.title: Data Security Pro-Tip ✅
slides.bubble: For true erasure, use special software or physically overwrite the data many times. Stay secure!

takeaway: Deleting a file only removes its address. The actual data stays on your disk until new information physically writes over it, making recovery possible!
caption:
🧠 DID YOU KNOW? 🤯

Your "deleted" files are actually still on your hard drive! They don't vanish into thin air.

Here's the mind-blowing reality:
🔹 When you hit 'delete,' your computer only removes the *pointer* (like a bookmark) to the file, not the file itself.
🔹 The actual data remains on your disk until new information physically overwrites those exact sectors.
🔹 This means old, 'deleted' data could potentially be recovered using specialized tools if not properly sanitized!
